title: Birds & Botanicals
description: The art of scientific observation — Audubon's birds and the great botanical plates.

items.title: Great American Shrike
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell meticulously depicts the Great American Shrike, showcasing the artist's skill in combining line and aquatint. The detailed rendering of the bird on ivory wove paper serves as both scientific illustration and fine art.
items.tags: bird, engraving, ornithological, nature, scientific illustration, printmaking, natural history

items.title: John James Audubon discovering his drawings eaten by a rat
items.description_narrative: This vibrant color woodblock print captures naturalist John James Audubon's dramatic discovery of a rat consuming his invaluable avian drawings. The vivid scene, characteristic of the medium, portrays a moment of profound artistic and scientific loss.
items.tags: john james audubon, rat, naturalist, discovery, woodblock print, 19th century, dramatic, frustration

items.title: Harlequin Duck
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: This vibrant hand-colored engraving captures the distinctive Harlequin Duck, showcasing intricate detail through aquatint and etching techniques. Created by Robert Havell, it exemplifies the detailed natural history illustrations of the early 19th century.
items.tags: harlequin duck, bird, wildlife, natural history, engraving, aquatint, etching, hand-colored

items.title: Black Backed Gull
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This print, titled 'Black Backed Gull,' is a meticulous ornithological illustration by Robert Havell. Created through hand-colored engraving with aquatint and etching, the artwork captures the bird's form and plumage with precise line work and subtle tonal variations.
items.tags: ornithology, bird, nature, engraving, aquatint, hand-colored, printmaking, detailed

items.title: Male Bay Breasted Warbler
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on cream wove paper
items.description_narrative: This exquisite hand-colored engraving by Robert Havell vividly captures the intricate details of a male Bay-breasted Warbler. Rendered with aquatint on cream wove paper, the print showcases the bird's distinctive plumage and a delicate branch.
items.tags: bird, warbler, nature, engraving, hand-colored, ornithological illustration, 19th century

items.title: Florida Jay
items.medium: Hand-colored engraving, with aquatint, on ivory wove paper
items.description_narrative: Robert Havell's 'Florida Jay' is a meticulously hand-colored engraving, capturing the distinctive plumage of the Florida Scrub-Jay. This detailed aquatint print exemplifies the artistic and scientific precision characteristic of early 19th-century ornithological illustration.
items.tags: bird, wildlife, natural history, engraving, hand-colored print, scientific illustration, 19th century

items.title: Cervus Virginianus
items.description_narrative: This hand-colored lithograph by John Woodhouse Audubon vividly portrays the Cervus Virginianus, commonly known as the white-tailed deer, with careful attention to naturalistic detail. The intricate rendition and hand-coloring highlight the animal's features, reflecting the era's focus on detailed natural history illustration.
items.tags: deer, wildlife, animal illustration, lithography, hand-colored, 19th century, natural history

items.title: Saint James the Greater
items.medium: Etching in black on cream laid paper
items.description_narrative: This etching in black on cream laid paper depicts Saint James the Greater, an important figure in Christian tradition. Created by the artist known as Master F. P., the print showcases the precise lines achievable through this medium.
items.tags: saint james, religious, christian, etching, printmaking, figurative, devotional

items.title: Bust of a Youth (Saint John the Baptist)
items.medium: Marble on variegated black marble socle
items.description_narrative: Francesco Mochi's marble 'Bust of a Youth' vividly portrays Saint John the Baptist, capturing a moment of profound spiritual intensity. The dynamic carving of the youthful figure, along with its expressive face, exemplifies the dramatic potential of Baroque sculpture.
items.tags: sculpture, marble, baroque, religious, saint john the baptist, bust, dramatic, expressive

items.title: Saint John the Evangelist
items.description_narrative: This etching by Paolo Farinati depicts Saint John the Evangelist, showcasing the characteristic linework of the printmaking medium. Created in 1567, it reflects the artistic approaches of its era.
items.tags: saint, biblical, etching, printmaking, renaissance art, religious, italian art

items.title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold—Southampton Water
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas by James McNeill Whistler captures the tranquil expanse of Southampton Water under a moonlit or twilight sky. Through a masterful blend of blues and golds, Whistler transforms the landscape into an ethereal study of atmosphere and color harmony, emphasizing beauty over literal depiction.
items.tags: nocturne, seascape, aestheticism, atmospheric, tonalism, blue and gold, tranquility

items.title: James William Wallack
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Charles Robert Leslie depicts James William Wallack. Created between 1835 and 1840, it showcases Leslie's skill as a portraitist.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 19th century, male figure, charles robert leslie, james william wallack, american art, british art

items.title: Plaque with Saints James and John the Evangelist
items.description_narrative: This plaque depicts Saints James and John the Evangelist, crafted from gilt copper with champlevé enamel. The intricate enamelwork, created by carving recesses into the metal and filling them with colored glass paste, exemplifies the decorative artistry of its period.
items.tags: religious, medieval, champlevé, enamel, metalwork, saints, decorative arts

items.title: At Mouquin's
items.description_narrative: William Glackens's 'At Mouquin's' captures a lively restaurant interior, depicting patrons engaged in dining and conversation. Rendered in oil on canvas, this 1905 work exemplifies a candid observation of urban life.
items.tags: restaurant, urban life, genre scene, american art, ashcan school, early 20th century, social realism

items.title: Butterfly
items.description_narrative: This delicate drawing, titled 'Butterfly,' is rendered in graphite by James McNeill Whistler, capturing the subtle form of the insect. Executed on ivory wove paper, it exemplifies a precise and refined approach to natural observation.
items.tags: butterfly, insect, drawing, graphite, sketch, nature, study, aesthetic

items.title: Head of Executioner, from John Evelyn's Sculptura
items.medium: Mezzotint in black on ivory laid paper
items.description_narrative: This mezzotint depicts the powerful "Head of Executioner," rendered in stark black on ivory laid paper. Created by Richard Houston in 1755, it showcases the detailed textural qualities possible with this printmaking technique.
items.tags: executioner, head, portrait, mezzotint, printmaking, 18th century, british
